To begin, let us address the setup. You should stand with your feet hip-width apart, ensuring the barbell is positioned over the mid-foot. When you hinge at the hips to grip the bar, keep your chest up and your back flat. The grip should be just outside your knees. Before lifting, take a deep breath into your belly to brace your core, and pull the slack out of the bar by standing up slightly before initiating the lift. This ensures the bar moves in a straight vertical path.

Regarding the pull itself, drive through your heels and push the floor away with your legs. Keep the bar close to your shins throughout the ascent. As the bar passes your knees, continue to push your hips forward until you are standing fully upright. Do not lean back at the top; simply stand tall with your shoulders over your hips. The descent should be controlled, hinging at the hips first to lower the bar past your knees, then bending your knees to return the weight
